messages.subject: Declaring variables ordinal "ordered=T"
parts:
I had a problem on my final involving ordinal data in lavaan. 
We had talked about the two ways (that I knew about) to declare variables ordinal. Then a student used syntax like this:

q1runT.out<-sem(q1runmod,q1ordinal,ordered=T)

and it seems to work. All observed variables were treated as ordinal. The documentation does not describe a logical option for ordered. Am I having delusions, or is this just not documented?

By the way, str(q1ordinal) confirms that each variable is integer, not factor or ordered factor.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Declaring variables ordinal "ordered=T"
parts:
On 12/17/19 10:25 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> I had a problem on my final involving ordinal data in lavaan.
> We had talked about the two ways (that I knew about) to declare
> variables ordinal. Then a student used syntax like this:
>
> q1runT.out<-sem(q1runmod,q1ordinal,ordered=T)
>
> and it seems to /work/. All observed variables were treated as ordinal.

> The documentation does not describe a logical option for ordered. Am I
> having delusions, or is this just not documented?

My mistake. It is a fairly recent change. I did mention it in the
version history of 0.6-4, but I forgot to update the man pages:
ordered = TRUE is simply a shortcut for ordered = names(myData).

I have now updated the man pages in lavaan dev 0.6-6.1508

Yves.
